questions.question: Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parwez Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Pathar Ki Masjid, also known as** Saif Khan's Mosque**, **Chimni Ghat mosque**, and **Sangi Masjid**, is a mosque in Patna, Bihar, India.
 
• It was built in **1621 by Parvez Shah,** the son of Mughal emperor **Jahangir**.
 
• The mosque is built of stone, hence the name "**Pathar ki Masjid**".
 
• It is located on** Ashok Rajpath** between Sultanganj and Alamganj.
 
• The mosque is a single-domed structure with four minarets.
 
• The central dome is supported by** four arches**.
 
• The mosque is a fine example of Mughal architecture.
 
• Pathar Ki Masjid is a beautiful and historic mosque that is an important part of the cultural heritage of Patna.
 
• It is a popular tourist destination and a place of worship for the Muslim community.

questions.question: If the price elasticity of demand is less than one, then the demand for the goods is said to be ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inelastic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Demand - 

 
 
• ​Demand means quantity demanded by customers at different prices during a given time period.
 
 
 
• Inelastic Demand:
 
 
• When due to change in price (whether increase or decrease), quantity demanded remains same, it is known as inelastic Demand.
 
• In case of inelastic Demand, when the price is increased, it will cause the total expenditure of the consumer to increase because total expenditure = quantity demanded × price.
 
• The demand will not change but the change in price cause consumer's total expenditure to increase.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Perfectly inelastic**

 
 
• A perfectly inelastic demand has an **elasticity of 0**.
 
• A perfectly inelastic demand is one when there is no change in the demand for a product with a **change in its price**.
 
• For a perfectly inelastic demand, the demand curve is represented as a **straight vertical line**.
 
 
 
• **Perfectly elastic**
 
 
• When a small change in the price of a product causes a major change in its demand, it is said to be** perfectly elastic demand**.
 
• In perfectly elastic demand, a small rise in price results in a fall in demand to** zero**, while a small fall in price causes an increase in **demand to infinity**.
 
• In such a case, the demand is perfectly elastic or **e = ∞**.
 
 

 
• **Unitary elastic**

 
 
• The demand curve for unitary elastic demand is a rectangular hyperbola.
 
• When the proportionate change in demand produces the same change in the price of the product the demand is referred to as unitary elastic demand.
 
• The elasticity of a unitary elastic demand is 1.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Industrial Policy resolution 1956?

I. This resolution formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan.

II. This policy was used for promoting industry in backward regions.
questions.solution:
Te correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956

__
 
• Adopted to achieve the aim of a socialist state with the government controlling the major strategic industries of the economy.
 
• According to this resolution, industries were classified into the following three categories:
 
 
• Category 1: Those industries that were established and owned exclusively by the public sector.
 
• Category 2: Those industries in which the public sector would perform the primary role while the private sector would play the secondary role i.e., the private sector supplements the public sector In these industries and new units could be set up only by the public sector.
 
• Category 3: Those industries that are not included in Category 1 and Category 2 were left to the private sector.
 
• The government kept indirect control of the industries in the private sector through the policy of industrial licensing.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Highlights of IPR 1956:__
 
• In order to initiate a new industry or expand existing capacity, private entrepreneurs were supposed to obtain licenses from the government.
 
• Licensing, imposition of the tax, tax exemptions, and subsidies were used by the government:
 
 
• to regulate private industries.
 
• bring about a reduction in regional disparities in industrial development. 
 
• to keep a check on the production of goods that are socially undesirable.
 
 
 
• Hence, the government fully controlled the private sector either directly or Indirectly through the IPR 1956.

questions.question: Which of the following seasons in India is known as the transition season?

questions.question: At places the groundwater is stored between layers of hard rock below the water table. This is known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **an aquifer**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• An aquifer is an underground layer of porous rocks or permeable rocks that store and retain groundwater levels in the soil.
 
• The underground aquifer is built with all types of porous or permeable rock materials, such as sand, gravel, or silt, making it a suitable water absorber.
 
• The rainwater enters the aquifer through the soil and becomes a part of the groundwater.
 
• The groundwater from the aquifers then resurfaces from springs and wells.
 
• We can also extract the aquifer water with the help of a water well.
 
• The study of groundwater, aquifer, and their property is known as hydrogeology.

 [IMAGE: https://media.nationalgeographic.org/assets/photos/000/191/19125.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**Pond:

 
• A pond is an area filled with water, either natural or artificial, that's lower than a lake.
 
• Defining them to be lower than 5 hectares (12 acres) in area, lower than 5 measures (16 ft) deep, and with lower than 30 emergent foliage helps in distinguishing their ecology from that of lakes and washes.

Lake:

 
• A lake is an area filled with water, localized in a basin, surrounded by land, and distinct from any river or other outlet that serves to feed or drain the lake.

Well:

 
• A well is an excavation or structure created in the ground by digging, driving, or drilling to access liquid resources, usually water.

questions.question: In humans, the digestion of carbohydrates like starch, begins in which of the following parts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Buccal cavity**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**The human digestive system consists of two parts, the alimentary canal, and the associated glands.

__
 
• The mouth leads the food to be digested to the buccal cavity.

 
 
• The buccal cavity has a number of teeth and a muscular tongue.
 
• The uppermost part of the buccal cavity is called the palate.
 
• The digestion of carbohydrates begins in the buccal cavity.
 
 
 
• From the mouth, food reaches into the stomach through a food pipe called the esophagus.
 
• There is no digestion inside the food pipe.
 
• The digestion of fat begins in the stomach.
 
 
• Lipase is the digestive enzyme of fat.
 
 
 
• The digestion of protein occurs in the stomach and duodenum.
 
 
• Pepsin is the digestive enzyme of protein.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Digestive system:

 
• It consists of the long alimentary canal and associated glands.
 
• The alimentary canal includes
 
 
• Mouth (buccal cavity)
 
• Oesophagus (food pipe)
 
• Stomach
 
• Small intestine
 
• Large intestine
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b905d7003d06f4639a74ccbd24f9cf2bdcff2761f7ec676a8d5b9d6de2e57d19.png] 

The glands associated with the digestive system are as follows: 

 
• Liver 
 
• Pancreas 
 
• Intestinal glands

questions.question: _______ is a tributary of river Godavari.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Indravati**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry (Yanam).
 
• The other names for the Godavari River are The Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• Godavari river drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Godavari river originates from Bramhagiri mountains at Trimbakeshwar.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner, and the Sabri.
 
• The longest tributary- The Manjira
 
• The largest tributary- The Pranhita

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcf92b48b809c3eb721c9fed87b753c04217e0130f42e4de80a9af2dcc680ed2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Chambal:**

__
 
• The Chambal river originates in Manpura near Indore in Madhya Pradesh.__
 
• The length of the river is 900 km and it is a tributary of the Yamuna river.
 
• The Chambal River remains one of North India’s unpolluted rivers, home to a rich diversity of flora and fauna.
 
• The National Chambal Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for the rare Ganges river dolphin.
 
• Apart from the Ganges river dolphin, the other inhabitants of the sanctuary include magar (crocodile) and gharial (alligator). Migratory birds from Siberia form part of its rich avian fauna.

**Banas:**

__
 
• Banas river originates from Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range, near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, Rajasthan. '
 
• Banas river is a tributary of the Chambal River and ii is approximately 512 kilometers in length.
 
• This river is also called ‘Van Ki Asha‘.
 
• There is another river in Rajasthan with name of Banas.
 
• The Banas river entirely flows within the Rajasthan in:-
 
 
• Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Dausa, Jaipur, Pali, Rajsamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk, and Udaipur districts of Rajasthan. 
 
 
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.

**Tawa:**

 
• Tawa River is the tributary of the Narmada River__.
 
• It is the longest tributary of the Narmada River.
 
• Its origin is in the Satpura range.
 
• It meets the Narmada at Hoshangabad district.
 
• Its length is 172 km.

questions.question: Which union territory of India has a sea named after it?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**

The elongated chain of islands located in the Bay of Bengal extending from north to south is called Andaman and Nicobar islands. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**Andaman and Nicobar islands:

__
 
• Andaman and Nicobar Islands situated in the Bay of Bengal, run like a narrow chain in the north-south direction extending between 6° 45′ N to 13° 45′ N.
 
• This archipelago is composed of around 265 big and small islands (203 Andaman islands + 62 Nicobar Islands)
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands extend from 6° 45′ N to 13° 45′ N and from 92° 10′ E to 94° 15′ E for a distance of about 590 km.
 
• The total area of this elongated island is 8,249 sq. km.
 
• The Andaman islands are divided into three main islands i.e. North, Middle, and South.
 
• Duncan's passage separates Little Andaman from South Andaman.
 
• The Great Andaman group of islands in the north is separated by the Ten Degree Channel from the Nicobar group in the south.
 
• The Grand Channel is between the Great Nicobar islands and the Sumatra islands of Indonesia.
 
• The Coco Strait is between the North Andaman islands and the Coco Islands of Myanmar.
 
• Port Blair, the capital of Andaman Nicobar Islands lies in the South Andaman.

 
• Among the Nicobar islands, the Great Nicobar is the largest.
 
• It is the southernmost island and is very close to Sumatra island of Indonesia.
 
• The Car Nicobar is the northernmost.
 
• Most of these islands are made of tertiary sandstone, limestone, and shale resting on basic and ultrabasic volcanoes.
 
• The Barren and Narcodam Islands, north of Port Blair, are volcanic islands

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Puducherry:

 
• There are total 4 Districts in Puducherry.
 
• The city is surrounded by Tamil Nadu state, on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, 105 miles (170 km) south of Chennai (Madras).
 
• The Union Territory of Puducherry has been formed consolidating four erstwhile French establishments viz Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.
 
• Karaikal District is in the state of Tamil Nadu and is next to Puducherry in area and population. 
 
• Mahe is surrounded by the State of Kerala and Yanam by the state of Andra Pradesh.
 
• Yanam is one of the regions in the Union Territory of Puducherry which is 870 km away from it.
 
• The town of Yanam lies on the mouth of the Godavari River where it flows into the Bay of Bengal.

'Daman' is the capital of the Union Territory of Daman and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu are part of the union territory.

questions.question: Who emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (Formless) in Punjab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Baba Dayal Das'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Nirankari is a religious reform movement within Sikhism.
 
• The Nirankari movement was founded by Baba Dayal Das in 1851.
 
• He believed that God is formless, or nirankar (hence the name Nirankari).
 
• The movement expanded in northwest Punjab. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Baba Ram Singh:

__
 
• **Baba Ram Singh** was born in the year **1815.**
 
• He was a son of a poor carpenter, in a small village of Bhaini.
 
• Which was around 7 kilometers away from Ludhiana.
 
• In the early 1840s, he served as a soldier in the** Sikh Army of Prince Naunihal Singh.**
 
• He left the army after the overthrow of the Sikh rule.
 
• In the year 1838, he came in contact with Baba Balak Singh, and he also remained in touch with Bhagat Jawar mal as well.

 Guru Gobind Singh__

Birth:

 
• He was born on December 22 in Patna in the year 1666.
 
• His birth anniversary is observed as Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti every year in accordance with the lunar calendar. 
 
• He was a poet, spiritual leader, philosopher, warrior and writer.
 
• 10th Guru:
 
 
• He was the tenth Guru of the Sikhs.
 
 

Khalsa Panth:

 
• He was the founder of the Khalsa Panth. 

 
 
• He also founded the Sikh warrior community called Khalsa in 1699.
 
 
 
• He became a Sikh guru at the age of nine, after the death of his father Guru Tegh Bahadur.
 
 
• His father was executed by Aurangzeb.
 
 

Five K's

 
• He introduced the five K's for the Sikhs including:

 
 
• Kesh: uncut hair
 
• Kangha: a wooden comb
 
• Kara: an iron or steel bracelet worn on the wrist
 
• Kirpan: a sword 
 
• Kacchera: short breeches.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of "term - sport" is NOT correct?

I. Batting - Cricket

II. Goal - Netball
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Both pairs are correctly associated. Batting is a term used in cricket, and a goal is a term used in netball.
 
• Here are tables of important terms related to cricket and netball:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terms related to cricket.**

 
 

 Term
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Batting
 The act of hitting the ball with the bat in an attempt to score runs.
 
 

 Bowling
 The action of the player throwing the ball towards the wicket defended by the batsman.
 
 

 Run
 The basic unit of scoring in cricket, achieved by batsmen running between the wickets.
 
 

 Wicket
 The set of stumps and bails; also refers to the dismissal of a batsman.
 
 

 Over
 A set of six deliveries bowled by the same bowler from the same end of the pitch.
 
 

 Innings
 The period in which a team or a batsman is at bat.
 
 

 Duck
 A score of zero by a batsman.
 
 

 Century
 A score of 100 runs by a batsman in a single innings.
 
 

 Maiden Over
 An over in which no runs are scored off the bowler's deliveries.
 
 

 Out
 The condition when a batsman is dismissed from play.
 
 

 
• **Terms related to Netball.**

 
 

 Term
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Goal
 A successful shot in the opponent's net, worth one point.
 
 

 Centre Pass
 The method of starting and restarting play at the beginning of each quarter and after a goal is scored.
 
 

 Wing Attack
 The position that links the attack and centre court, feeding the ball to the shooters.
 
 

 Goal Circle
 The semi-circular area in front of each goal from within which goals may be scored.
 
 

 Footwork
 The rule that states a player may land and then pivot on one foot while in possession of the ball.
 
 

 Free Pass
 A pass awarded after an infringement by the opposing team.
 
 

 Offside
 An infringement that occurs when a player moves out of their designated area.
 
 

 Penalty Pass
 A free pass awarded where the infringement occurred.
 
 

 Pivot
 A player using one foot as a swivel while moving the other foot in any direction.
 
 

 Throw in
 A method of restarting play when the ball has gone out of court.

questions.question: In Kheda, Gujarat, Patidar peasants organised non-violent campaigns against which of the following demand of the British?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __High land revenue__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Patidar peasants in Kheda, Gujarat, organized non-violent campaigns against the British primarily** due to their demand for** high land revenue.**
 
• This was** one of the key issues that led to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, **a significant event in the **Indian independence movement, which was led by figures like Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, Vallabhbhai Patel, and others.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Kheda Satyagraha__

 
 
• In the middle of the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Gandhi also got involved in the Ahmedabad textile mill strike.
 
• Here his adversaries were the Gujarati millowners.
 
• The immediate reason for the industrial conflict was the withdrawal of plague bonus, which was being given to dissuade workers from leaving the city in the face of mounting plague-related deaths.
 
• Also, it was during Ahmedabad textile mill strike that Gandhiji for the first time during the Indian National Movement took fast unto death( to strengthen the workers‘ resolve).
 
• Hence his first hunger strike was during Ahmedabad Strike and not at Kheda.
 
• The cause for Kheda Satyagraha was that the peasants of Kheda district were in extreme distress due to a failure of crops and that their appeals for the remission of land revenue were being ignored by the Government.
 
• Discontinuation of the Plague bonus was the immediate cause for Ahmedabad textile mill strike.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies the composition of the Council of States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __80.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Rajya Sabha or Council of States is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• Composition/Strength of Rajya Sabha:
 
 
• Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250.
 
• Out of 250 seats of Rajya Sabha, 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the two Union Territories. 
 
• The present strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, out of which 233 are representatives of the States and Union territories of Delhi and Puducherry and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• The members nominated by the President are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in respect of such matters as literature, science, art and social service. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States):

 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the creation of a ‘Council of State’ as a second chamber of the then legislature.
 
• Rajya Sabha is the Upper house of the bicameral Parliament of India.
 
• Allocation of Seats:
 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the allocation of seats to the States and Union Territories in Rajya Sabha. 
 
• The allocation of seats is made on the basis of the population of each State.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lok Sabha:

 
 
• Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution defines the composition of the House of the People or Lok Sabha.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 550.
 
• Out of 550 seats of Lok Sabha:
 
 
• Up to 530 members represent the States
 
• Up to 20 members represent the Union Territories 
 
 
 
• The house currently has 543 seats, which are filled by the election of up to 543 elected members.

questions.question: Which city will host the 2032 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Brisbane__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• American executive Cindy Hook has been appointed as the inaugural **CEO of the organising committee for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Brisbane.**
 
• The organising committee announced the appointment on** December 13 after engaging with 50 candidates over six months.**
 
• Hook was based in Singapore as **CEO of Deloitte Asia Pacific until June and had previously worked for the international professional services network in the US and in Australia, moving to Sydney in 2009 to lead the auditing practice for six years and later becoming CEO of the Australian operation in 2015.**
 
• The International Olympic Committee awarded the **2032 Games to Brisbane in July of last year, under a revamped procedure for choosing host cities that saw a small group of IOC members identify and propose host cities to the board.**
 
• **Australia has twice previously hosted the Summer Olympics, at Melbourne in 1956 and Sydney in 2000.**
 
• **The 2032 organizing committee held its first board meeting in April and, on** July 23, started the decade-long countdown.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **2032 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the XXXV Olympiad and also known as Brisbane 2032, **will be an international multi-sport event scheduled to take place from **23 July to 8 August 2032, in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia.**
 
• Following changes in the bidding rules, the **International Olympic Committee selected and announced Brisbane as the winning bid on 21 July 2021, two days before the start of the 2020 Summer Olympics.**

questions.question: The Natya shastra which provides information regarding musical instruments is compiled by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Muni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Natya Shastra,** an ancient Indian treatise on the **performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance and music, is traditionally attributed to Bharata Muni.**
 
• It provides information about musical instruments, **as well as a wide range of other subjects related to the performing arts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amir Khusrau:**

 
 
• A legendary figure in Indian music and culture, **Amir Khusrau was a 13th-century Sufi musician, poet, and scholar from India.**
 
• He has been** credited with introducing several musical styles and instruments to Indian music, such as the qawwali and the sitar.**
 
• Khusrau served in the court of several **Delhi sultans and is known for his contributions to Hindustani classical music.**
 
 
 
• **Tansen:**
 
 
• Tansen, originally named Ramtanu, was a prominent figure of Hindustani classical music in the medieval period.
 
• He was a **court musician in the darbar (court) of the Mughal Emperor Akbar.**
 
• His contributions to Indian music include compositions in** Dhrupad, one of the oldest genres of Hindustani classical music.**
 
• Many** legends are associated with his musical prowess.**
 
 
 
• Kalidas:
 
 
• Kalidas was a classical Sanskrit writer and is often considered ancient India's greatest playwright and poet.
 
• His notable works include plays like** Abhijnana Shakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala) and epic poems like Raghuvamsha (The Dynasty of Raghu).**
 
• However, he is not directly associated with musical instruments or treatises on music.

questions.question: In FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, the opening match was played between Morocco and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazil beat Morocco 1-0 **in the opening match of the **2022 FIFA U-17 World Cup at the Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar.**
 
• The national football federation has never provided an explanation for the choice, however, there are many theories.
 
• Some stated the All-India Football Federation (AIFF) could not afford to send the players to Brazil at the time, while some claimed it was because the team intended to play barefoot.
 
• The 32 football games of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 were played at three locations. 
 
• The DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra; the Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao, Odisha.
 
• It took place at Navi Mumbai.
 
• At the Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar, the seventh **FIFA U17 Women's World Cup got underway on October 11, 2022.**
 
• On October 30, the championship game was placed at the DY Patil Stadium.
 
• **Spain**, **defending champions** won the **FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup against the first-time finalists Colombia**.** FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup was played between Spain and Colombia in the Patil Sports Stadium**.
 
• India hosted the competition for the first time this year and made their debut.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The FIFA Under 17 Women's World Cup took place in **India in 2022.**
 
• It was the first time the nation has hosted a competition from the women's world football governing body.
 
• This is the third-most significant Women's Competitions event on the FIFA calendar, featuring 36 games between 16 nations at 5 locations in India.
 
• One of the most significant tournaments ever to be organised in Indian football history, the FIFA Under 17 Women's World Cup has served as a crucial starting stone in the careers of several international football heroes.
 
• The FIFA Under 17 Women's World Cup had a long-lasting impact on Indian football, modernising the facilities, establishing suitable operational guidelines, and raising the level of play in general.
 
• Unquestionably, the FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup in India in 2022 has the potential to revolutionise Indian football.
 
• With an expected global audience of around 200 million people from almost 200 different nations, the tournament has a significant impact on the entire world.
 
• This presents India with a fantastic opportunity to showcase its cities, culture, and capacity to host events of the greatest calibre.

questions.question: Kailash Satyarthi has received the Noble Prize in the field of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Kailash Satyarthi 

 
 
• Kailash Satyarthi is an Indian social activist who works and campaigned against child labour in India and elsewhere and advocated the right to education. 
 
• In 2014 he was the recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize, along with Pakistan Malala Yousafzai,** “for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education”.**
 
• Kailash Satyarthi founded the movement called Bachapan Bachao Andolan in India. Hence statement B is correct. 
 
• Kailash Satyarthi is the fifth Indian Nobel prize winner. 
 
 

 
• Other Noble Prize winners from India:__

 __
 
• Rabindranath Tagore
 
• Chandrashekhar Venkataraman 
 
• Mother Teresa 
 
• Amartya Sen
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The*** 2025 Nobel Prizes ***were awarded across five categories, highlighting achievements in quantum physics, materials science, immunology, literature, and peace.

 
 
• **Physics Prize:**

 
 
• Awarded to** John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis** for their work in **macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits**, showcasing quantum mechanics at a macroscopic scale.
 
• Their work enabled advances in quantum computing, cryptography, and quantum sensors.
 
 
 
• **Chemistry Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to** Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar M. Yaghi** for their development of **metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), materials with vast internal surface areas** for various applications such as water harvesting, carbon capture, and toxic gas storage.
 
 
 
• **Medicine Prize**:
 
 
• Awarded to **Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi **for **discovering regulatory T cells (Tregs) that prevent autoimmune diseases** and play a role in cancer therapy.
 
• Their work has revolutionized the understanding of autoimmune diseases and immunotherapy.
 
 
 
• **Literature Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to L**ászló Krasznahorkai **for his** visionary works, including "Satantango**", which explore themes of apocalyptic terror, chaos, and human isolation.
 
• Known for long, complex sentences and dark, philosophical narratives.
 
 
 
• **Peace Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to **Maria Corina Machado**, a** Venezuelan leader **and symbol of democratic resistance against authoritarianism in Venezuela, emphasizing "ballots over bullets" and leading the opposition.
 
• Praised for her courage despite life-threatening risks and for unifying the opposition around democratic principles.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Distribution:**

 
 
• United States leads with six laureates.
 
• Other countries: Japan (2 laureates), Australia, Hungary, and Venezuela (1 laureate each).
 
 
 
• **Ceremony:** 
 
 
• The award ceremony will take place on December 10, 2025, in Stockholm (Peace Prize in Oslo).
 
• Each prize includes 11 million Swedish kronor, a gold medal, and a diploma.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding coal is NOT correct?

options.text: Anthracite is the highest quality hard coal.
Coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperatures is bituminous coal.
Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content.
Metallurgical coal is high grade lignite coal which has a special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metallurgical coal is high-grade lignite coal **which has a special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces,** this statement is NOT correct.**
 
• Metallurgical coal**, also known as coking coal, is a high-quality hard coal (not lignite) used to produce coke, which is necessary for iron smelting in blast furnaces.**
 
• Metallurgical coal **needs to have low sulfur and phosphorus contents, making it much rarer and more valuable than thermal coal, which is used to produce heat and electricity.**
 
• **Typically, bituminous coal or anthracite is used for this purpose, not lignite, which is lower-grade coal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anthracite is the highest quality hard coal:**

 
 
• **Anthracite is indeed the highest grade of coal.**
 
• It's the oldest type of coal, having spent the most time underground exposed to pressure and heat.
 
• It's very hard and shiny** (hence "hard coal") and burns cleanly with little soot, making it much cleaner than other types of coal.**
 
• It's less common than other forms, which makes it more expensive.
 
 
 
• **Coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperatures is bituminous coal:**
 
 
• Bituminous coal is a medium-rank coal between sub-bituminous coal and anthracite.
 
• It has been subjected to higher pressures and temperatures than lignite and sub-bituminous coal, but not as much as anthracite.
 
• **Bituminous coal is commonly used for generating electricity and heating in industrial processes.**
 
 
 
• **Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content:**
 
 
• Lignite, often referred to as brown coal, is indeed a low-grade coal.
 
• **It's softer than bituminous coal or anthracite, and it has a high moisture content.**
 
• This makes it less energy-dense and more polluting than higher-grade coals.
 
• **Lignite is often used in electricity production in power plants located near mining sites.**
